title: Loops: While and For
description: Learn how to repeat code with loops. Master while loops, for loops, and control statements like break and continue.
objectives: Write while loops for condition-based repetition
Use for loops for counting iterations
Control loop flow with break and continue

sections.title: Why Loops?
Loop Syntax Comparison
sections.explanation: BPL uses 'loop' for both while-style and for-style loops, making it consistent and simple.

sections.title: While Loop (Condition-Based)

lineExplanations.8: loop (condition) - keeps running while condition is true.
lineExplanations.10: IMPORTANT: Update the loop variable or you'll loop forever!

sections.title: For Loop (Counter-Based)

lineExplanations.6: Three parts: initialization; condition; update. Variable 'i' is local to loop.
lineExplanations.13: Increment by 2 instead of 1 to get even numbers.

sections.title: Break: Exit Loop Early
sections.expectedOutput:
Finding first number > 50 divisible by 7:
Found: 56
Checking 1... nope
Checking 2... nope
Checking 3... nope
Checking 4... nope
Checking 5... nope
Checking 6... nope
Checking 7... Found it!

lineExplanations.10: break immediately exits the loop, jumping to after the loop.
lineExplanations.23: Use break when you've found what you're looking for.

sections.title: Continue: Skip to Next Iteration

lineExplanations.8: continue skips the rest of this iteration and goes to the next.
lineExplanations.10: This line only runs for odd numbers (evens are skipped).

sections.title: Infinite Loop (with break)
sections.expectedOutput:
Infinite loop with break:
Iteration 1
Iteration 2
Iteration 3
Breaking out!
Attempt 1: Invalid, try again
Attempt 2: Invalid, try again
Attempt 3: Valid input!

lineExplanations.10: loop { } without a condition runs forever.
lineExplanations.25: Infinite loops are useful for input validation.
lineExplanations.14-17: ALWAYS have a break condition in infinite loops!

sections.title: Nested Loops

lineExplanations.15: Inner loop runs completely for each outer loop iteration.
lineExplanations.24: The inner loop runs 'row' times, creating the triangle shape.
lineExplanations.13-19: Outer loop handles rows, inner loop handles columns.

sections.title: Common Loop Pitfalls
Practice: Sum of Numbers
sections.instructions:
Write a program that:
1. Calculates the sum of numbers from 1 to 10
2. Prints each number as you add it
3. Prints the final sum (should be 55)
sections.hint: Use a running total variable, start at 0, add each number in the loop.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
sections.content:
✅ **loop (condition)** - while-style loop, runs while condition is true

✅ **loop (init; cond; update)** - for-style loop with counter

✅ **loop { }** - infinite loop (must use break to exit)

✅ **break** - exit the loop immediately

✅ **continue** - skip to the next iteration

✅ Always update your loop variable to avoid infinite loops!

questions.question: How many times does this loop run? loop (local i: int = 0; i < 5; i = i + 1) { }
questions.explanation: i goes through values 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 (5 iterations). When i becomes 5, the condition i < 5 is false.

questions.question: What does 'break' do?
questions.explanation: break immediately exits the loop and continues with code after the loop.

questions.question: What does 'continue' do?
questions.explanation: continue skips the rest of the current iteration and moves to the next one.
